text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract ended a thinly traded after hours session just below resistance at 92.250 and where a break could spark a further rapid rally.
*U.S. Treasuries flat ahead of refunding auctions.
The Australian 10-year bond futures contract ended a thinly traded after-hours session just below resistance at 92.250 and where a break could spark a further rapid rally, traders said.
The contract ended the SYCOM session at 92.245, up slightly from Monday's firm 92.230 close and after holding 92.205 amid initial weakness in U.S. Treasuries in New York on Monday.

The long-end of the market has shaken off some of its recent negativity after breaching major resistance at 92.210/92.230 during Monday's advance, but 92.250 is proving a stiff barrier again, having capped the contract in April.

The long end of the market is starting to build in the prospect of a bond-friendly budget on May 13, while the short-end has lost some of its direction after last week's strong wages data killed off hopes of a monetary policy easing.
The Reserve Bank holds its monthly policy meeting today, although economists do not expect it to endorse a policy change.
The June three-bond futures ended SYCOM one basis point higher at 93.18, with the contract seen capped at 93.210/93.230.
"We expect the yield curve to continue to flatten to around 80 basis points as policy easing trades are unwound," one trader said.
The three/10-year bond futures spread ended Monday's session at around 93 basis points having retreated from a recent peak of 106 basis points in late April.
U.S. Treasuries ended Monday's session flat as the market squared positions ahead of the first leg of the refunding auctions later on Tuesday when US$17.0 billion of three-year notes will be offered.
A further US$12.0 billion of five-year notes will be offered on Wednesday.
